$comment: Violation ratchet for gates whose dead scan root was repaired. A repair REVEALS pre-existing debt; it does not create it. Each entry records the count revealed at repair time — the gate fails only when its count RISES. Lowering a count is a normal commit; raising one is a defect. Entries expire: a baseline that has not dropped within 56 days of `landed` (or of `reaffirmed.date`) fails its gate, because a number that never moves is suppression with extra steps. Mechanism + rationale: src/scripts/_lib/gate_baseline.ts. Decision: AI council 2026-08-02, roadmap road-to-gates-that-can-fail blocker `dead-gate-finding-triage`.

ci-parity:local-only.note: Gates that `task ci` runs and no workflow does — the direction this manifest's own header calls the one that let real defects merge (16 stale index rows reached the trunk behind a local-only check-index). Revealed, not created, by repairing the checker's extraction: check_ci_local_parity built its CI-side set by regexing RAW workflow text for `task <name>` and expanding each closure, comments included. Several workflow comments contain the literal string `task ci` while stating that no workflow invokes it, so `ci` was read as an invocation and its full 247-gate closure entered the 'runs in CI' set. The count was therefore 0 BY CONSTRUCTION, and the prose documenting the gap was what suppressed it. Measured at the repair: CI-side 273 → 106, undeclared_local_only 0 → 167 of 247 local gates (68%). Baselined rather than hard-failed because 167 findings nobody can clear in the change that reveals them is the gate-that-lands-as-N-instant-blockers failure this repository has refused before; shrink-only keeps the property that matters, namely that a NEW gate registered in `task ci` with no workflow reds immediately. Lowering happens by wiring gates into workflows or declaring them under `local_only:` with a reason. Note the punchline, because it bounds the risk of this entry: check_ci_local_parity ITSELF runs in no workflow, so it is its own finding and this ratchet has no remote reach either — clearing the backlog is what gives it teeth. DRAINED BY ONE, 2026-08-13: check_ci_local_parity itself was wired into consistency.yml, so it left the set it exists to report. That is the whole shape of a legitimate drain here — the gate stops being local-only because a workflow now runs it, not because the declaration list grew. The floor in gate-coverage.yml moved in the same change and for the same reason: wiring two gates raised the parsed population 357 -> 360 (109 CI + 251 local). The intermediate 359 was the reading after the CI-side wiring alone and before check_gate_coverage joined the local `ci` chain; it was committed here by mistake and is corrected rather than left as a second number for the same measurement.

check_no_new_legacy_path:hardcoded-scan-.note: Lines under src/scripts/**/*.{ts,mts,mjs} that pass the retired `.agent-src.uncondensed` directory into `path.join(...)` — a filesystem path CONSTRUCTED against the tree ADR-051 abandoned, which is the exact shape of all 14 dead gates. Deliberately narrow so the number is signal, not noise: 236 raw mentions under src/scripts → 147 string-literal lines → 67 path-constructing lines when the pass was written, after exempting src/scripts/_lib/agent_src.ts (the shared resolver, whose job IS owning the constant — gates that route through it survived the move). Detectors holding the literal as data to match, strip, or print are not counted, and no prose, docs, tests or fixtures are read: that full-tree shape was measured at 44 files / 213 hits and rejected as the wrong lint (see the note in check_no_new_legacy_path.ts::find_offenders). Recorded at 58 rather than 67 because Phase 1's scan-root repairs were landing on this branch while the pass was being written and had already removed 9 — a baseline above the truth silently permits new violations. This count goes to ZERO as the remaining repairs land; every repair is a lowering commit. Lowered 56→51 by the road-to-renewal-foundation Phase 1 dead-root sweep (check_always_budget, check_portability, check_references, lint_framework_leakage, lint_agents_md). Lowered 51→49 by the gate-hardening adoption PR: skill_collision_clusters and skill_overlap were repointed at the live skills tree via the shared resolver — two gates that had been reading the retired container and scoring 0 of 288 skills. Lowered 49→48 by road-to-rule-delivery-integrity P2.2: score_skill_selection was repointed at the live skills tree via the shared resolver. It is the same shape as the two gates lowered before it — a scorer reading the retired container and scoring 0 of 288 skills — and here the consequence was sharper than a dead gate: the roadmap's pre-registered selection-accuracy criteria would have been compared against a baseline of silent zeros. Lowered 48→47 on 2026-08-13, and this one is a catch-up rather than a repair: the pass reported 47 against a baseline of 48, so a gain had already landed without the ratchet following it. Attributed to 455160160 (fix(evals): resolve the eval orchestrator against the live skills tree), the most recent repair in this branch's base that removes a path-constructing line — SKILLS_ROOT repointed through _lib/agent_src.ts::SRC_SKILLS(). A loose ratchet is not harmless: it silently permits one new violation to be added back without any gate noticing, which is the shape this entry exists to prevent.

audit_user_type_axis.note: One orphan user-type value: `legal`. Five legal-review-prep skills (contract-review, dpa-review, nda-triage, legal-intake-triage, legal-practice-profile) declare `recommended_for_user_types: [legal]`, but there is no `user-types/legal.yml` — the pack shipped an axis value with no user-type definition behind it, and the dead scan root hid it (the audit reported used=0 orphans=0 while reading zero skills; it now reads 288 and reports used=8). Clearing this entry is a product call, not a copy edit: either author `user-types/legal.yml` (tagline, recommended packs, install-path hint) or drop `legal` from those five skills. Not decided here because both options change shipped pack behaviour.

lint_handoffs.note: All 18 are `handoff_tier_mismatch`: a senior-tier skill links to a peer whose frontmatter carries no `tier` (reported as tier='unset') — e.g. build-buy-partner → adr-create, customer-research → po-discovery, gated-reach → threat-modeling. This is a tier-metadata backfill backlog on the LINKED-TO skills, not a broken link. The one genuinely dangling link revealed by the same repair (competitive-positioning → a non-existent ../analyze-reference-repo/SKILL.md; it is a command, not a skill) was FIXED in the repairing commit rather than baselined. Clearing this entry means backfilling `tier` on the linked-to skills, or deciding that `tier: unset` on a link target is not a violation and narrowing the rule.

lint_roadmap_blockers:decidability.note: Open blocker entries that are not yet DECIDABLE by the person who owns them — missing `Recommendation:` (which option and why), missing `If you do nothing:` (the cost of the non-decision), or a `What to do:` carrying no command, path or enumerated option set. Revealed by adding the decidability half to lint_roadmap_blockers, not created by it: the five original fields describe a situation and never made it actionable, so a blocker could pass the contract while handing the analysis back to the person least equipped to redo it. Measured at introduction: 36 open entries, ALL 36 undecidable, and 14 of the 46 total entries carry no command/path/option at all in `What to do`. Baselined rather than hard-failed because 36 findings nobody can clear in the change that reveals them is the gate-that-lands-as-N-instant-blockers failure this repository has refused before — the same reasoning as ci-parity:local-only above. First measured at 34 rather than 36 because the two blockers on the branch that introduced this (`ac3-false-positive-reading`, `publish-side-marker-invariant`) were rewritten to the new standard and then closed in the same change; a baseline above the truth silently permits new violations. Re-measured at 38 when the branch was re-pointed at current main, and the +4 is population growth rather than a loosening: main gained the four `road-to-inbox-harvest-2026-08-d-*` roadmaps (context-ledger, runtime-skill-routing, scheduled-deprecation, top-band-model-economy), each carrying one open blocker authored before this requirement existed. That is the honest number for the population this gate now scans — recording 34 against a 38-entry tree would have failed the gate on its own introducing commit and taught the next reader to distrust it. Lowering happens one blocker at a time, and every roadmap touched for other reasons is a chance to lower it. Lowered 38→37 by the scheduled-deprecation PR, which is exactly that shape: code-graph-removal-authorisation was rewritten to the new standard because the roadmap was being touched anyway. Its `If you do nothing:` is one of the few that is not the common no-cost answer — the release gate that PR ships refuses the next major cut while the blocker is open, which is the field doing the work it was added for. The 56-day expiry is the point, not a hazard: if this number has not moved in two months, the fields are not being written and the gate should fail until someone decides whether the requirement is real. Lowered 37→34 when the scheduled-deprecation branch merged current main: three blockers were resolved or rewritten on the trunk in the meantime, so the drop is a genuine drain plus a merge, not a loosening. Re-tightened here rather than left loose because a ratchet that lags its own tree permits violations back in silently.

lint_pack_boundaries.note: Markdown links between source artefacts that cross a pack boundary the source pack's `requires` graph does not reach — revealed when the scan root moved off the deleted packages/ tree to the live corpus (0 -> 753 artefacts scanned). 82 distinct pack pairs across 131 source files; largest single class is engineering-base -> meta (73), skills in a consumer-installable pack citing this package's own maintenance skills. Each is a link that dangles for a consumer who installs the source pack without the target's. Judged real drift rather than an over-strict gate because it is long-tailed — top bucket 22%, no single systematic cause — unlike the lint_artefact_frontmatter case, where one required shape had 0-of-288 adoption. Fix per finding: add the edge to packs.yml requires, retarget the link, or move the artefact.

check_gate_completeness.note: Ledger adoption ratchet. 216 of 244 registered gates do not yet carry per-target completeness accounting (`_lib/gate_ledger.ts`) or a `// ledger-exempt:` marker. This is deliberately NOT a sweep: road-to-skill-ecosystem-gate-integrity Phase 1 adopts exactly three gates (lint_framework_leakage, check_references, lint_roadmap_complexity) plus the checker itself to prove the interface, and the remainder migrates as gates are touched. Shrink-only from here — the number may not grow, so a NEW gate must adopt or exempt.

check_depth_budget.note: Four depth files exceed the 16,000-char per-file ceiling: rule-body-migration-inventory.md (23,782), design-antipatterns.md (20,707), roadmap-process-loop.md (20,360), orchestration-telemetry.md (16,155). Recorded rather than fixed because splitting four large reference documents is unrelated to the change that introduced the ceiling, and a gate that lands as four instant blockers is the shape this repository has already recorded as a failure. Shrink-only from here: a FIFTH over-ceiling file reds. roadmap-process-loop.md is the file that motivated the gate — it states 'Size budget: <= 4,000 chars' in its own header and is 5x over it, which is what a declared budget with nothing measuring it decays into. The ceiling is a GROWTH RATCHET, not a measured quality threshold: the 7,308-trajectory study behind the 3,500-token skill ceiling (ADR-217) was taken on procedural always-co-loaded skills, and this layer is declarative and loaded one or two files at a time. Replace the number when someone measures comprehension on THIS layer.

gate-self-test:registered-non-adopters.note: Self-test adoption ratchet, expressed as a shrink-only NON-adopter count. 24 of the 32 gates registered enforced in gate-coverage.yml carry neither a `--self-test` (`_lib/gate_self_test.ts`) nor a `// self-test-exempt: <reason>` marker, so nothing proves they DISCRIMINATE — an enforced `scanned:` floor proves a gate read something, only a self-test proves the reading changes the verdict. Deliberately NOT an adoption column ratcheted upward: check_gate_coverage.ts's own report_hardening_ratchet rejects that shape in this same file ("grades the solution instead of the problem"), and the sibling adoption ratchet (check_gate_completeness) is already a non-adopter count. Population is the manifest, not every script under src/scripts: padding the manifest to move this number would mean adding a floor per row. Shrink-only from here — a NEW registered gate must adopt or exempt. Migration mechanism, same as the ledger ratchet above: gates adopt as they are touched, not in a sweep — the eight current adopters were each added alongside a real change to that gate. The 56-day non-stagnation clause applies unchanged, so a count parked here fails on its own.

lint_settings_classes:derivable-surface.note: Anti-regrowth ratchet for the settings disposition axis. 83 of 134 template leaves are classified `derivable` — the mechanism can decide from the situation, so the key should not exist — and each names the replacement that would decide instead (`lint_settings_classes` rejects the bare label, which is what keeps the class from becoming a synonym for "inconvenient to keep"). This is a DELETION QUEUE, not 83 deletions: a row stays until the mechanism it names actually exists, and deleting a key ahead of its mechanism is a silently-changed default rather than a simplification. Shrink-only from here, which is the anti-regrowth half — a NEW key classified `derivable` raises the number and reds, so a key whose answer the situation already carries cannot be added at all. The 56-day non-stagnation clause is the other half and is wanted here rather than tolerated: a queue that never drains is a stated direction nobody is walking. The queue opened at 88 of 140 on 2026-08-12 and drained to 83 of 134 the same day: six keys had no reader whatsoever (telegraph.speak_scope, chat_history.max_size_kb, chat_history.on_overflow, quality.wait_for_remote_ci, screenshots.data_bearing_gate, legal_review_prep.consented_at), five of them `derivable` and one a `consent` row reclassified because a published-egress confirmation is a Hard Floor no setting may lift. An unread key is the only deletion that cannot silently change a default, which is why that batch went first. The classification itself is docs/contracts/settings-classes.md.
